Condon’s Frolics

It does sound very similar to Sliabh Russell to me, though.

Condon’s Frolics

Reading through a Spanish phrase book a few days ago, I found something very funny about the title of this jig. Sorry, I won’t go into detail. Just use your imagination.

As far as I know, pipers like to play this in Ador, but it’s commonly played in Edor, especially in Clare and Galway.

# Posted on June 5th 2009 by olciamis ~ whose English is much better than my Polish…

My english demands polishing because I’m polish. Joke. But please, concentrate and try to understand=)

I haven’t known it for this name by myself. But I have started my adventure with a celtic music with the album Cuilidh by Julie Fowlis and I found this recording here https://thesession.org/recordings/2919, and then I saw the track 6 (not only) is not described yet. The first jig was named The Thatcher, so I accepted this name and tried to write notes.
Condon’s Frolics is actually the same tune. But it demands to connect it with Julie Fowlis>Cuilidh>track 6>1st jig
